description: We are Selenova1.0, a team passionate about space exploration, astronomy, and technology. Our project, Lunar Landing Site Navigator, aims to identify safe lunar landing locations using terrain analysis and intelligent navigation. We bring curiosity, creativity, research, and problem-solving skills. We are looking for teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, GIS, satellite imagery, physics, or UI/UX design. Let's make lunar exploration safer!
summary: Selenova1.0 is an interactive lunar landing site navigator designed to identify safe, scientifically valuable touchdown zones on the Moon. Using high-resolution elevation, slope, and illumination datasets from NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), Selenova1.0 evaluates lunar terrain against critical mission parameters such as surface roughness, solar visibility, and proximity to permanently shadowed regions (PSRs). Addressing the challenges of autonomous hazard avoidance and lunar resource utilization, the platform processes topographical maps to generate real-time hazard heatmaps and optimal landing trajectories. As global space agencies prepare for sustained lunar presence under programs like Artemis, selecting safe landing sites is vital for protecting landers, rovers, and crewed missions from treacherous craters and steep slopes. Selenova1.0 transforms complex planetary telemetry into an intuitive decision-making tool for mission planners, researchers, and educators.
details:
Selenova1.0 is a geospatial navigation and terrain-analysis platform for lunar descent planning. Users select a target region on the Moon—such as the Lunar South Pole—and set mission constraints including maximum allowable slope angle, minimum solar illumination duration, and target proximity to water-ice deposits. Selenova1.0 overlays NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) imagery with Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) digital elevation models to compute safety scores across candidate landing ellipses, highlighting hazards like boulders, steep crater rims, and permanent shadows.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

1) Risk Reduction: Minimizes landing hazards by automatically filtering out terrain with dangerous slopes or poor lighting conditions.

2) Mission Optimization: Balances engineering safety with scientific return by pinpointing safe zones near high-interest geological features and potential In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) sites.

3) Accessibility: Makes open NASA planetary data accessible and easy to visualize for students, researchers, and mission designers.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

1) Frontend / Visualization: React, Three.js / WebGL, HTML5/CSS3. Backend /

2) Data Processing: Python, NumPy, GDAL / Rasterio.

Rather than displaying static maps, Selenova1.0 combines multi-layer orbital telemetry into a dynamic, weighted scoring engine. Our team factored in real aerospace engineering constraints—including lander tilt tolerances, power generation needs from solar angles, and direct-to-Earth communication line-of-sight—to simulate realistic mission trade-offs.
